paper.title: Online Learning with Feedback Graphs Without the Graphs

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial setting with never-revealed feedback graphs (self-loops present) (lower bound)
unmapped: Feedback graphs may be chosen jointly with (correlated with) the losses
Learner only observes out-neighbourhood of chosen action; graph never revealed
settings.definition_quote: In the adversarial setting, the loss vectors $\ell_1,...,\ell_T$ and the feedback graphs $G_1,\ldots,G_T$ are chosen by the environment in an arbitrary way. ... The feedback graph $G_t$ itself \emph{is never revealed} in its entirety to the learner.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic setting with never-revealed feedback graphs (self-loops present)
unmapped: Loss vectors drawn i.i.d. from a joint distribution over [0,1]^K, independent of the arbitrary graph sequence
settings.definition_quote: In the stochastic setting, the environment privately selects a loss distribution $\D$ over $[0,1]^K$ and an arbitrary sequence $G_1,\ldots,G_T$; thereafter, the loss vectors $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T$ are sampled i.i.d.~from~$\D$.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial setting, strongly observable hidden graphs without guaranteed self-loops (lower bound)
unmapped: Learner need not observe her own loss (self-loops optional)
Graphs may be correlated with losses
settings.definition_quote: we no longer assume that the learner automatically gets to observe the loss of the action that she chose. Instead, we allow the graphs to have self-loops

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic setting, strongly observable hidden graphs without guaranteed self-loops
unmapped: Learner need not observe her own loss (self-loops optional)
settings.definition_quote: In the stochastic setting, there exists an online learning algorithm that attains $\tO(\sqrt{\alpha T})$ regret, provided that $G_1,\ldots,G_T$ are all strongly observable.

unmapped: Learner need not observe her own loss
settings.definition_quote: In the stochastic setting, there exists an online learning algorithm that attains $\tO(K^{1/3} T^{2/3})$ regret, provided that $G_1,\ldots,G_T$ are all observable.

conditions: all feedback graphs have independence numbers <= O(1) (at most 9 in the construction)

source.label: thm:main-lower
source.quote: In the adversarial setting, any online learning algorithm must suffer at least~$\Omega(\sqrt{KT})$ regret in the worst case, even when all feedback graphs $G_1,\ldots,G_T$ have independence numbers $\le O(1)$.

results.notes: Proof gives sqrt(KT)/64 for the conditioned environment. Regret compares to v* minimizing expected cumulative loss.

conditions: against the specific randomized construction (Bernoulli losses, random graphs correlated with loss of v*)

source.label: thm:lowerbound
source.quote: Assume that $K \ge 2$ and $T \ge K^2$. Any deterministic learner must suffer an expected regret of at least $(1/32) \sqrt{K T}$ against the environment constructed above.

results.notes: Graph independence numbers bounded only w.h.p. (Lemma 5); Theorem 1 uses conditioning.

symbols.alpha_G: upper bound on the independence numbers of all feedback graphs G_1..G_T (not known to the learner)

conditions: independence numbers of all G_t at most alpha

source.label: thm:alg1regretbound
source.quote: Assume that $K \ge 2$. Suppose that \cref{alg:stochastic} is run on a sequence of feedback graphs with independence numbers $\le \alpha$. Then the expected regret of the algorithm is at most $\tO(\sqrt{\alpha T})$.

results.notes: Also stated as Theorem 2. Proof gives O(sqrt(T alpha log K log^2(KT))). Algorithm does not need alpha.

symbols.sum_Vtau: sum over V^(tau), the tau = ceil(10 alpha log K) suboptimal actions with smallest gaps
symbols.alpha_G: bound on independence numbers of all feedback graphs

conditions: independence numbers of all G_t at most alpha

source.label: thm:alg1gapbasedregretbound
source.quote: Suppose that $K \ge 2$ and $T \ge K$, and let $\tau = \lceil 10 \alpha \log K \rceil$. Suppose that \cref{alg:stochastic} is run on a sequence of feedback graphs with independence numbers  $\le \alpha$. Then the expected regret of \cref{alg:stochastic} is at most \[ \O\lr{ \sum_{v \in V^{(\tau)}} \frac{1}{\Delta_v} \log T } ~. \]

source.label: thm:stronglylowerbound
source.quote: In the adversarial setting, any algorithm must suffer at least~$T / 16$ regret in the worst case, even when $G_1,\ldots,G_T$ are all strongly observable.

symbols.alpha_G: bound on independence numbers of all feedback graphs

source.quote: In the stochastic setting, there exists an online learning algorithm that attains $\tO(\sqrt{\alpha T})$ regret, provided that $G_1,\ldots,G_T$ are all strongly observable.
In the stochastic setting, there exists an online learning algorithm that attains $\tO(K^{1/3} T^{2/3})$ regret, provided that $G_1,\ldots,G_T$ are all observable.
